readback.name: Poincare.DeTurckJetRealization.exists_compact_symmetric_realization
readback.mathematical_statement:
Let E = EuclideanSpace R (Fin 3), Bilin = E ->L[R] E ->L[R] R, Jet1 = E ->L[R] Bilin and Jet2 = E ->L[R] Jet1, with the Euclidean norm on E and the canonical iterated continuous-linear-map operator norms on Bilin, Jet1 and Jet2. The four local instances explicitly install the normed additive group and real normed space structures for the two jet spaces. For every function h : E -> Bilin, every point z : E and every set U : Set E, assume U is open, z belongs to U, h is ContDiffAt R (2 : WithTop ENat) at z, and eventually in nhds z every pair v,w : E satisfies h(y)(v)(w) = h(y)(w)(v). The symmetry assumption is one neighborhood germ valid simultaneously for all tensor-slot pairs; it does not assume h symmetric globally. The C2 assumption is at z, not a global boundedness, compact-support, or global C2 assumption.

There then exists a scalar function eta : E -> R satisfying all eleven ordered conclusions: (1) eta is ContDiff R ((top : ENat) : WithTop ENat), hence C-infinity in the all-finite-orders sense; (2) eta has compact support; (3) tsupport eta is contained in U; (4) eta is eventually exactly 1 in nhds z; (5) the specified function realized eta h z is C-infinity with the same order convention; (6) it has compact support; (7) its tsupport is contained in U; (8) for every y,v,w : E it is symmetric in v,w; (9) its value at z equals h(z); and (10) its first real Frechet derivative at z equals fderiv R h z; and (11) its second real Frechet derivative at z equals fderiv R (fderiv R h) z. More literally the last portion of the conjunction is three equalities: realized eta h z z = h z; fderiv R (realized eta h z) z = fderiv R h z; fderiv R (fderiv R (realized eta h z)) z = fderiv R (fderiv R h) z. Each derivative equality is an equality of the full continuous linear maps, respectively in Jet1 and Jet2, not merely diagonal values or tensor entries. No derivative slot is discarded or reordered.

The pinned definition fixes the witness field rather than allowing an arbitrary smooth replacement. Put J0 = fderiv R h z and H0 = fderiv R (fderiv R h) z. Then polynomial z (h z) J0 H0 y = h(z) + J0(y-z) + (1/2) * H0(y-z)(y-z), as an equality in Bilin, and realized eta h z y = eta(y) * that polynomial. Consequently in tensor slots v,w its value is eta(y) * [h(z)(v)(w) + J0(y-z)(v)(w) + (1/2) * H0(y-z)(y-z)(v)(w)]. H0 has two ordered spatial derivative slots followed by the two tensor slots. The original ordered H0 is used in the quadratic term; there is no stipulated replacement by a symmetrized jet. C2 at z makes the original second spatial derivative a genuine jet, and the eventual tensor-slot symmetry hypothesis is the one supplied assumption for the demanded global symmetry of the polynomial cutoff field.

HasCompactSupport means the topological support, the closure of the nonzero set, is compact. Both topological supports must lie inside the original open U, and eta must be identically 1 on a neighborhood of z. The scalar eta has no asserted nonnegativity, upper bound, sign, or prescribed formula. The smoothness order is the coerced ENat top, not the outer WithTop top. There is no quantitative bound in any norm, no Graph or Holder carrier, no positive-definiteness or invertibility conclusion, no manifold/chart or time parameter, and no approximation or density claim. In particular the conclusion matches exactly the value, first derivative and ordered second derivative at z; it does not require realized eta h z to equal h on a neighborhood of z.
